newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler, UAW set to end strike - NYT.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler, UAW set to end strike - NYT.

text.p: Negotiators from Chrysler Corp. and the United Auto Workers union have reached an agreement that will end a nearly month-long strike that has shut production of some high-profit vehicles, the New York Times said on Wednesday.

According to people close to the talks, junior negotiators were settling details late Tuesday but a broad pact was reached on a new labour contract at Chrysler's Mount Road plant in Detroit, the newspaper said.
People close to the talks were quoted by the Times as saying the final deal was inconclusive with room for each side to claim victory.
The Mount Road plant and other factories idled by the strike could return to operation by the end of this week, the Times said, citing people familiar with the negotiations.
Sources familiar with the situation told Reuters bargainers were scheduled to meet late Tuesday, indicating a possible break in the strike.
There had been next to no local talks since the strike began on April 9.
Chrysler was not available to comment.
The strike by 1,856 UAW members at the Mount Road engine plant has paralysed Chrysler's pickup truck and sport utility production. The walkout idled 18,916 workers.
Workers demanded Chrysler drop plans to shift production of drive shafts to an outside supplier, which the union said would cost it 300 jobs.
